svg.title: RabbitMQ request and reply
svg.desc: A sequence diagram of a command sent over RabbitMQ with a reply. The caller calls RabbitMqCommandBus.dispatchAndReceive (RabbitMqQueryBus.ask and dispatchAndWait work the same way). The OUTBOUND middleware runs in the sending process, then RabbitMqPublisher sends the request through RabbitTemplate.sendAndReceive to the cqrs.commands topic exchange, with the message name as routing key, the cqrs.message.type and cqrs.context headers, a reply-to address (Spring AMQP's direct reply-to, amq.rabbitmq.reply-to, by default) and a correlation id. The exchange routes it to the queue of the responding service, cqrs.stock.commands. RabbitMqCommandConsumer checks that the message is exposed, rehydrates the MessageContext from the headers, runs the INBOUND middleware and calls the handler. The result goes back to the reply-to address with the same correlation id, the requester matches it and converts it, with the ResultType when one was passed, and the caller receives it. The requester waits up to the reply timeout, spring.rabbitmq.template.reply-timeout (5 seconds by default) or cqrs.rabbitmq.commands.reply-timeout and cqrs.rabbitmq.queries.reply-timeout. Three outcomes: the handler returns, and a business refusal is returned as a result record such as Reservation(false, "no stock"); the handler throws, the error reply carries the cqrs.error and cqrs.error.type headers and the caller gets a RemoteHandlerException with the remote exception's type name and message only; or no reply arrives in time and the caller gets a RemoteReplyTimeoutException while the handler may still run or may have run, so it must be idempotent by business key. The animation plays the three outcomes in turn.
svg.text: dispatchAndReceive, dispatchAndWait and ask wait for the reply with their correlation id, up to the reply timeout
